items.instruction: Summarize this annual review in 4-5 sentences for an executive audience.
items.source: Annual review of the field operations programme. The programme began in 2023 with four regions and expanded to eleven by the end of 2025. Headcount grew from 22 to 71 over the same period, with the sharpest increase in 2024 when three regions were added simultaneously following the acquisition of a regional competitor. Training was standardised in early 2024 after inconsistent onboarding was identified as the leading cause of first-year attrition, which stood at 34% in 2023 and fell to 19% by 2025. Equipment costs per field technician fell from 84,000 to 61,000 rupees, largely through a consolidated procurement agreement signed in June 2024, though the agreement also reduced the range of available equipment, which two regional managers have flagged as a constraint for specialised jobs. Customer satisfaction for field visits held between 4.2 and 4.4 out of 5 throughout, with no clear trend. Average time to complete a standard installation fell from 3.1 hours to 2.4, attributed roughly equally to the standardised training and to a route planning tool introduced in late 2024. Two regions, North East and Central, consistently underperform on completion time, both averaging above 3 hours; a review found both cover unusually large geographic areas rather than having process problems. Scheduled maintenance visits, which were 12% of workload in 2023, are now 31%, reflecting the maturing installed base, and this shift is the main driver of the 2026 headcount request. The programme has not yet measured revenue impact of maintenance visits separately from installations, which the finance team has raised twice.
items.gold:
must_include: ['expanded from 4 to 11 regions and 22 to 71 headcount over 2023-2025', 'first-year attrition 34% to 19% after training standardisation', 'installation time 3.1 to 2.4 hours from training plus route planning tool', 'maintenance visits grew 12% to 31% of workload, driving the 2026 headcount request', 'revenue impact of maintenance not yet measured separately, raised twice by finance']
must_not_include: ['North East and Central have process problems', 'customer satisfaction improved']
reference: The field operations programme expanded from four regions to eleven and from 22 to 71 staff between 2023 and 2025. Standardised training cut first-year attrition from 34% to 19%, and installation time fell from 3.1 to 2.4 hours through a combination of that training and a route planning tool. Consolidated procurement lowered per-technician equipment costs from 84,000 to 61,000 rupees, though it narrowed equipment choice in ways two regional managers say constrain specialised work. Customer satisfaction was flat throughout at 4.2-4.4. The structural shift is in workload mix — maintenance visits rose from 12% to 31% — which drives the 2026 headcount request, but their revenue impact has never been measured separately, a gap finance has raised twice.
items.probes: long input near context pressure; key points distributed across the whole text
items.gold_notes: Hard because signal is distributed and several figures are decoys at executive level. The finance measurement gap is the item most often dropped; its absence is a coverage failure. Attributing North East / Central underperformance to process rather than geography is a faithfulness failure.
items.response_text:
**Executive Summary:**

The Field Operations Programme expanded significantly from 2023 to 2025, growing from four to eleven regions and increasing headcount from 22 to 71 employees, with the largest expansion in 2024 following a regional acquisition. Standardized training reduced first-year attrition from 34% to 19%, while equipment costs per technician decreased by 27% through a consolidated procurement deal, though this has limited equipment options for specialized tasks. Customer satisfaction remained stable (4.2–4.4/5), and average installation time improved from 3.1 to 2.4 hours due to training and route optimization, though two regions lag due to geographic challenges. Maintenance visits now account for 31% of workload (up from 12%), driving the 2026 headcount request, while revenue impact from maintenance remains unmeasured—a gap finance has flagged. Overall, the programme has scaled efficiently but must address regional inefficiencies and financial tracking to sustain growth.

Text:
Setting up a read replica takes about twenty minutes if you have the connection details to hand. Start by creating the replica instance in the same region as your primary — cross-region works but adds replication lag you will feel later. Next, copy the primary's connection string into the replica configuration and set the replication user, which needs only the read and replication grants, never write. Then start the initial sync and watch the lag counter; it should fall to under a second within a few minutes on a small database. Finally, point your reporting queries at the replica hostname and leave writes going to the primary. If lag climbs steadily instead of settling, the usual cause is a long-running transaction on the primary holding the log open.

items.source: The onboarding redesign shipped to 50% of new accounts on 12 June. Over the following four weeks, completion of the setup flow rose from 54% to 67%. Time to first meaningful action fell from a median of 19 minutes to 11. However, day-30 retention was statistically indistinguishable between the two groups, which the team did not expect. Qualitative follow-up suggested the redesign helps users finish setup but does not change whether the product fits their need. Two segments diverged: self-serve accounts improved most, while accounts arriving via partner referral showed no completion improvement at all, possibly because they arrive with different expectations. The team recommends shipping to 100% on the completion gains alone, while treating retention as an unrelated problem.
